deck: The shifts are real and mostly hormonal. Knowing which is which makes them easier to work with.
description: What changes in skin after 40 — collagen, oil, hydration, and menopause — explained plainly.

public.body: Skin in your forties is not failing. It is running on a different hormonal budget, and a few informed adjustments go a long way.

Collagen production slows, so skin loses some of its bounce. Oil glands quiet down, so skin that was once shiny turns dry. Around menopause, falling estrogen accelerates both — often noticeably, over a couple of years.
public.title: What shifts

items: A richer moisturizer, because the skin no longer makes as much of its own oil.
Daily sunscreen, which prevents far more visible aging than any serum reverses.
A retinoid, the best-studied ingredient for collagen — started slowly.
public.title: What helps most

public.body: None of this is about turning back a clock. It is about giving skin the support it used to make for itself. That is a reasonable, achievable goal.
